claims.text: Current experimental and computational methods have limited accuracy for determining the specified melting and liquid-state thermodynamic properties of multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
Current experimental and computational methods provide limited availability of the specified melting and liquid-state thermodynamic properties.
Current experimental and computational methods have limited efficiency across large high-entropy-alloy composition spaces.

A CALPHAD-based high-throughput computational method can improve the accuracy of determining melting temperature, fusion enthalpy and entropy, melting volume change, and liquid thermodynamic properties relative to current baselines.
A CALPHAD-based high-throughput computational method can improve the availability of those thermodynamic properties.
A CALPHAD-based high-throughput computational method can improve the efficiency of determining those thermodynamic properties.
The method can determine melting temperature for multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
The method can determine enthalpy and entropy of fusion for multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
The method can determine volume change upon melting for multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
The method can determine liquid thermodynamic properties for multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
CALPHAD-based high-throughput computation can efficiently screen thousands of alloy compositions.
High-throughput CALPHAD enables rapid exploration of a vast high-entropy-alloy compositional space.
CALPHAD can investigate composition and temperature effects on high-entropy-alloy microstructure.
CALPHAD calculations require computational software and a thermodynamic database.
The proposed intervention applies broadly to high-entropy alloys in both high-temperature solid and liquid states.
Prediction performance is limited by CALPHAD accuracy and thermodynamic-database quality.
Significant deviation between CALPHAD predictions and experimental data would falsify the hypothesis.
